problems.name: Rice blast
problems.summary: A fungal disease that causes lesions on leaves, stems, and grains.
symptoms: Diamond-shaped brown spots on leaves with gray centers
Dead leaf tips in severe cases
problems.causes: Fungus Magnaporthe oryzae; spreads in warm, humid weather with heavy dew.
remedies: Apply fungicides labeled for rice blast where permitted; follow label rates.
Remove heavily infected debris after harvest where practical.
prevention: Ensure good field drainage and spacing for airflow.

problems.name: Brown planthopper
problems.summary: A sucking insect that can cause hopper burn and virus spread.
symptoms: Honeydew and sooty mold on plants
High insect counts at base of plants
problems.causes: Outbreaks often follow overuse of nitrogen or indiscriminate pesticide use that kills natural enemies.
remedies: Follow integrated pest management: scout weekly, treat only when above threshold.
Use approved insecticides as a last resort per local guidance.
prevention: Conserve beneficial insects; avoid broad-spectrum sprays unless needed.

problems.name: Cassava mosaic disease
problems.summary: Viral disease causing leaf mottling and stunted growth.
problems.causes: Viruses transmitted by whiteflies and infected cuttings.
remedies: Uproot severely infected plants and use clean planting material from trusted sources.
prevention: Control whitefly populations with cultural practices where effective.

problems.name: Fall armyworm
problems.summary: Caterpillar pest that damages maize leaves and whorl.
symptoms: Young larvae on underside of leaves
problems.causes: Moths migrate and lay eggs; larvae feed aggressively in warm seasons.
remedies: Scout early and treat according to local extension thresholds.
Use approved products per label and rotate modes of action where advised.
prevention: Conserve natural enemies; hand-pick egg masses in small plots if feasible.
